data.source: coltrane main @ 0.8.0 (c3a942d) — inline node repro against dist/src, run 4x, identical every run
data.minimal_case: Register domain type `change-context` (extends Signal, required_fields: ["claims"]). Define agent `read-context` (SENSE, output_types: ["change-context"]). Compose standard `software-change-v1` with one phase `sense-context` holding one chair whose output_contract is ["change-context"]. Drive it with an invoker that returns exactly what the model emitted: ```json\n{"source": "repo://coltrane", "summary": "read the tree"}\n```  (valid JSON, no `claims`). Call `extractJson(MODEL_TEXT, {})` — it RETURNS the object, no throw, no schema check. Then `runGig(standard, {}, {outputs, ledger, invoke: () => parsed})` — it throws RuntimeError at seal and `outputs.all()` is empty.
data.steps:
1. `git log --oneline -1` → c3a942d (0.8.0); `dist/src/` present.
2. STEP 1 — the write boundary: `extractJson` (src/claude_invoker.ts:363, the sole return of the model-chair path at :698 and :737) returned {"source":"repo://coltrane","summary":"read the tree"}. `"claims" in parsed` === false. It did not throw. Grep of claude_invoker.ts confirms the only gates before this point are stream-level (#223 errorSubtype, apiErrorText, #222 empty-text) plus shape heuristics inside extractJson (fenced-wins, expectKeys narrowing, requireUnambiguous) — expectKeys only NARROWS candidate selection and never rejects; there is no output_contract/registry schema check anywhere on this path.
3. STEP 2 — the same predicate was already answerable at that instant: `outputs.validateWrite({core_type:"Signal", domain_type:"change-context", data: parsed})` → {"valid":false,"reason":"output rejected: change-context failed schema validation — required: must have required property 'claims' 'claims'; additionalProperties: must NOT have additional properties 'summary'"}. So the engine COULD have refused at the boundary; nothing on the model-chair path asks it to.
4. STEP 3 — end to end: `runGig(...)` threw RuntimeError from the post-hoc gate at src/runtime.ts:2252-2263 (`for (const {spec, slice} of resolved) deps.outputs.validateWrite(...)` → `Nothing was written — a chair's outputs are all-or-nothing.`).
5. STEP 4 — the damage: `outputs.all()` === [] . The whole chair aborted all-or-nothing; the agent that emitted the bad object had already exited, so the rejection reason reaches no one who could act on it.
6. Determinism: 4 runs total (1 verbose + 3 repeat), every run REPRODUCED with sealed:0. No network, no clock, no model spawn — the invoker is a pure function.

data.manifestation_site: src/claude_invoker.ts:417 — `return pool[pool.length - 1]!.value;` in `extractJson` (decl :363). This is the sole value-producing return of the model-chair path (reached from :737 stream / :698 customRun) and it hands an arbitrary `Record<string, unknown>` to the runtime as the chair's answer with no registry / output_contract schema check — despite `schema` for exactly that domain_type being in scope 80 lines earlier at src/claude_invoker.ts:657 and already spent on prompt prose (:199) and on key-narrowing (:667 → :447-458). The predicate that rejects the payload is available and answerable at that instant (reproduction STEP 2: validateWrite → {valid:false, reason:'…must have required property \'claims\''}); nothing on this path asks it. The observable failure surfaces two frames later at src/runtime.ts:2252-2264 (post-hoc gate) and is reported at src/runtime.ts:1542-1544, but that is the DETECTION site, not the defect site.
claims: The write boundary and the gate boundary are different code sites. The gate has exactly one owner — `checkWritable` (src/outputs.ts:515), exposed as a question by `validateWrite` (src/outputs.ts:892-893) and for effect by `write` (src/outputs.ts:638-639). The model-chair path calls neither until after the agent has exited.

`extractJson` (src/claude_invoker.ts:363-418) has three exits that throw — array-shaped output (:376), no JSON object at all (:386), ambiguous-with-no-schema (:410) — and one exit that returns (:417). None of the three throws is a CONTENT check; the schema is used only to pick BETWEEN candidates (`extractOptionsForChair`, :447-458, maps a schema's `required`/property names to `expectKeys`, and :400-406 explicitly notes the signal 'never widens and never picks a partial match' — it also never rejects).

The information needed to refuse is already resolved inside the invoker closure before the spawn: `sealTypes` (src/claude_invoker.ts:655), `outType` (:656), `schema = promptSchemaFor(registry, outType)` (:657), and `outputSchemas` for a multi-output chair (:660-662). The schema is spent on prose to the model (:199 'It must match this JSON schema') and on key-narrowing (:667) but never on validation of what came back.

The rejection reason is produced only after the producer is unreachable. `spawnStreaming` (src/claude_invoker.ts:705/752) is awaited to child exit before `extractJson` returns; the post-hoc gate runs at src/runtime.ts:2252 in a later frame. There is therefore no channel by which the refusal can reach the entity capable of repairing it — the failure is structural, not a missing retry.

The blast radius of enforcing late is the whole chair, by explicit design: #243's all-or-nothing seal (src/runtime.ts:2176-2185, 2239-2264) makes a single bad field abort every output the chair promised — the reproduction observed `outputs.all() === []`. Enforcing at the boundary is what would make the failure recoverable rather than total.

A validated in-band sibling exists and is bypassed. `output_write` runs the identical `checkWritable` through `outputs.write` (src/server.ts:643 → src/outputs.ts:638) and its refusal returns to a LIVE agent as `{ok:false, error}` via the dispatchTool try/catch (src/server.ts:411 / :2823). Note a secondary divergence found while reading: src/mcp.ts:170 declares output_write's `output_schema` as `{output_id, validation_result}`, but the handler returns `{output_id, primitive, output}` (src/server.ts:664) — `validation_result` is declared and never returned; the actual in-band signal is the thrown-then-caught error. Flagged for the sweep phase as a declared-contract/actual-return mismatch of the same family.

The same unvalidated boundary is reached by three further call sites that share `extractJson` and therefore share the class: src/bifrost_invoker.ts:127 (`extractJson(text, extractOptionsForChair(sealTypes, schema))` — same options derivation, same absence of a content check), src/document_factory.ts:119, and src/judges/user_flow_judge.ts:247 and :265 (which pass NO options at all). Candidate instances for the sweep phase; not yet checked-clean.

The t=0 preflight named in the defect report is NOT a still-open sibling of this shape: src/runtime.ts:1082-1133 already folds missing-skill-dir (:1090-1095), unknown-agent (:1102-1108), no-primitive (:1109-1114), no-output-type (:1115-1120) and tool-grant (:1121-1129) into one pre-spend sweep that throws `PreflightDispatchError` before any chair runs, with the mid-phase throws retained as unreachable backstops (:1080-1081). It is the CLOSED precedent for this class — the same 'move the refusal to the earliest point the predicate is answerable' move, applied to dispatch-time dead references — and the sweep should use it as the template, not re-open it.

data.violated_invariant: A typed contract must be adjudicated at the boundary where the payload ENTERS the engine as an answer — the earliest frame in which its predicate is answerable AND the producer is still alive to be told — not at the later boundary where the payload becomes durable. Coltrane names one owner of that predicate (`checkWritable`, src/outputs.ts:515, read this run) and mounts it only at the DURABILITY boundary (`write` :567 for effect, `validateWrite` as a question). The model-chair return boundary is an ingress that produces an engine-trusted answer without ever asking that owner, so the payload is trusted between two boundaries that are frames apart, and the refusal is computed at a point where nothing can act on it.
why_chain: 1. OBSERVED (defect report, corroborated by the runtime code read this run): the gig dies at `chair "read-context" cannot seal "change-context": output rejected: change-context failed schema validation — required: must have required property 'claims'. Nothing was written — a chair's outputs are all-or-nothing.` That exact string is emitted at src/runtime.ts:2258-2263.

2. WHY THERE — because src/runtime.ts:2252-2264 is the first and only place on the model-chair path that asks the seal predicate: `deps.outputs.validateWrite(...)` → src/outputs.ts:515 `checkWritable` → `registry.validate` (src/outputs.ts:567) → `{valid:false}`. The in-code comment at :2249-2251 states the intent plainly: 'validateWrite is the gate write runs, asked as a question instead.' The gate is correct and correctly placed for its own purpose; it is simply the FIRST asker.

3. WHY IS IT THE FIRST ASKER — because the model-chair path's own return boundary never asks. `extractJson` (src/claude_invoker.ts:363-418, read this run) has four exits: three throws — whole-text array (:376), no JSON object at all (:386), ambiguous-with-no-schema (:410) — and one return, `return pool[pool.length - 1]!.value;` (:417). All three throws are SHAPE/AMBIGUITY checks over the text. None is a CONTENT check against the output_contract. The single returning exit hands an arbitrary `Record<string, unknown>` to the runtime as the chair's answer.

4. WHY DOESN'T IT CHECK — because the schema is spent on selection, never on adjudication. `extractOptionsForChair` (:447-458) reduces the resolved schema to `expectKeys` (its `required` names, falling back to property names); `extractJson` :400-406 applies them only to narrow the candidate pool, and its own comment states the policy: the signal 'never widens, and it never picks a partial match'. Narrowing WHICH object is chosen is not rejecting the object chosen. A single-candidate emission missing `claims` therefore passes selection untouched.

5. WHY IS THIS PLACEMENT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT OF ONE MISSING CALL — because the ENFORCER, not merely a schema blob, is already in scope in that frame. `promptSchemaFor` (src/claude_invoker.ts:92-98) reaches `registry.effectiveSchema`, and src/registry.ts declares `validate(output)` at :61 and `effectiveSchema(slug)` at :71 on the SAME `Registry` interface — the very `validate` that `checkWritable` calls at src/outputs.ts:567. The invoker holds the object that owns the verdict and uses only its DESCRIBING half. Inside one closure: `sealTypes` (:655), `outType` (:656), `schema` (:657), `outputSchemas` (:660-662), the answer at `outcome.text` (:709), and the return at :737. Grep of src/claude_invoker.ts for /validate|retry|repair/ (this run) returns exactly two hits, both inside a comment at :229-230 noting that 'runtime.ts cannot currently tell a retryable parse failure from a non-retryable contract failure' — i.e. the file contains no validation call at all.

6. WHY THE CONTRACT WAS TREATED THIS WAY — because on this path the contract is stated as PROSE to the producer and never re-read as a PREDICATE over the product. `buildPrompt` embeds that same effective schema into the prompt ('It must match this JSON schema', src/claude_invoker.ts:199-202, per the unification note at :81-91), so the schema's whole role on the model-chair path is persuasive. A contract addressed only to the producer's intention, and never applied to the producer's emission, is unenforced by construction — compliance is left to the model.

7. WHY THAT MAKES THE FAILURE UNRECOVERABLE RATHER THAN MERELY LATE — because the producer is dead before the predicate is asked. `spawnStreaming` (:705) is awaited to child EXIT, `finalText` (:709) reads the corpse, `extractJson` (:737) returns, control leaves the invoker closure, and only two frames later does src/runtime.ts:2252 ask. There is no channel from the refusal back to the entity that could repair it. This is why no retry policy fixes the defect: retry re-runs a chair that was never told what was wrong.

8. WHY WE KNOW THE BOUNDARY IS ENFORCEABLE — because the engine already enforces it on the sibling ingress, and that one reaches a LIVE agent. `output_write` (src/server.ts:624-664, read this run) hands the caller's `data` straight to `deps.outputs.write` (:643), which runs the IDENTICAL `checkWritable` (src/outputs.ts:634-639) and throws; per the upstream defect-location (src/server.ts:411 / :2823, carried, not re-read this run) dispatchTool catches it and returns `{ok:false, error}` in-band to the still-running agent, which can repair and re-call. Same predicate, same payload shape, two ingresses — one adjudicated in the producer's lifetime, one not.

9. WHY THE BLAST RADIUS IS TOTAL — because late enforcement is composed with an all-or-nothing seal. src/runtime.ts:2176-2185 ('DECIDE BEFORE SEALING') and the gate at :2239-2264 deliberately make a chair atomic so a partial delivery cannot leave orphans. That design is right; but with the contract adjudicated only at that point, one absent field discards every output the chair produced, including the ones that were valid. Enforcing at ingress is what would make the failure recoverable instead of total.

10. ROOT — the engine's rule is 'one owner of would-a-seal-accept-this, mounted at the seal.' The unstated corollary it lacks is 'mounted at EVERY point a payload enters the engine as an answer.' The model-chair return boundary is such a point and has no mount, so it is the one write path that crosses unvalidated. The engine has already made exactly this move once, for a different defect class: the unified t=0 dead-reference preflight (src/runtime.ts:1063-1133, read this run) collects missing-skill-dir / unknown-agent / no-primitive / no-output-type / tool-grant into ONE pre-spend pass and throws `PreflightDispatchError`, explicitly retaining the mid-phase throws as 'unreachable backstops' (:1080-1081). Same shape — move the refusal to the earliest point the predicate is answerable, keep the late check as a backstop. That precedent covers dead REFERENCES at dispatch time; it was never extended to payload CONTRACTS at answer time.

criteria.test: Is the named cause upstream of the observed error, or is it the error's own site?
criteria.standard: A root must be a site whose correct behaviour would have prevented the observation; the detection site does not qualify.

criteria.test: Is the predicate ANSWERABLE at the proposed enforcement point in that frame?
criteria.standard: Every input the predicate needs must be provably in scope at the proposed site, from code read this run — otherwise 'enforce earlier' is a wish, not a cause.

criteria.test: Does the cause explain the RECOVERABILITY of the failure, not just its occurrence?
criteria.standard: The report's distinguishing complaint is 'no feedback to the already-exited agent'; a cause that explains only the rejection is a symptom-level cause.

criteria.test: Is the cause a class, or one instance?
criteria.standard: It must be statable as an invariant that a sweep can test other sites against, not as a fact about extractJson.

criteria.test: Is the cause immune to the obvious non-fixes (add a retry / strengthen the prompt / relax the schema)?
criteria.standard: If any of those would close it, the invariant named is the wrong one.

data.class_name: unadjudicated-ingress — an owned predicate mounted downstream of the frame that could act on it
data.frame: The instance is 'extractJson returns a contract-violating payload'. The class is NOT 'extractJson lacks a validate call' (that is one site) and NOT 'validation runs too late' (that is a timing complaint). The class is a PLACEMENT relation between two things the engine already has: an INGRESS (a frame where an externally-produced value becomes an engine-trusted value) and an OWNED PREDICATE over that value (checkWritable/registry.validate, resolveAgentGrants, composeStandard's dead-name rules). Coltrane's discipline is 'one owner per predicate' — src/outputs.ts:510-513, read this run, states it verbatim ('the one owner of "would a seal accept this"'). Single ownership is correct and is not the defect. The defect is that single ownership was implemented as single MOUNTING: the predicate is called at the one boundary its author cared about (durability, at src/outputs.ts:638; spend, at the write loop src/runtime.ts:2268) and at no other boundary a payload crosses. Every ingress between an unmounted crossing and the mount holds an engine-trusted value that no owner has adjudicated, and the mount lands after the producer is unreachable — so the verdict is computed at a coordinate where it can only abort, never repair. Read the class as a coordinate error (WHERE the owner is invoked), not an omission error (WHETHER an owner exists) — every instance found so far has the owner in lexical scope and consumes only its describing half.
data.class_shape:
A site is an INSTANCE iff all four conjuncts hold, each decidable by reading the site:

(1) INGRESS — the site converts a value it did not compute (a child's final text, a caller's payload, a recalled cache entry, a chart edge's seed, a genome file's bytes) into a value the engine subsequently treats as authoritative. Test: does an engine-trusted value flow OUT of this frame that came from outside it?

(2) OWNED PREDICATE EXISTS AND IS DECIDABLE HERE — the engine already owns a total predicate over that value, and every input the predicate needs is provably in scope in this frame. Test: name the owner (src/outputs.ts:515 checkWritable / src/registry.ts:61 validate / resolveAgentGrants / a composeStandard rule) and name the in-scope bindings it would take. data.killing_invariant:
EVERY BOUNDARY A PAYLOAD CROSSES AS AN ANSWER MUST BE ADJUDICATED BY THE PREDICATE'S ONE OWNER, IN THE EARLIEST FRAME WHERE THE PREDICATE IS ANSWERABLE AND THE PRODUCER CAN STILL ACT ON THE REFUSAL — AND NEVER FIRST AT THE FRAME WHERE THE PAYLOAD BECOMES IRREVERSIBLE.

Four clauses, each doing distinct work:
(a) ONE OWNER, MANY MOUNTS. Single ownership of a verdict is preserved (it is what stops two surfaces disagreeing, src/outputs.ts:512-513); what is forbidden is single MOUNTING. The owner is called at every crossing; the later call is retained as an unreachable backstop, never removed — exactly the discipline src/runtime.ts:1080-1081 already states for the t=0 preflight ('the mid-phase throws stay in place as unreachable backstops') and src/claude_invoker.ts:635 states for the per-chair grant guard.
(b) EARLIEST ANSWERABLE FRAME. Not 'as early as possible' — as early as the predicate is TOTAL. A predicate whose inputs are not yet knowable (a gig's runtime arguments at compose time) must not be mounted early; that is why gig-bound skill slots are correctly not compose time's business.
(c) PRODUCER STILL ALIVE. A refusal computed after the producer's exit is a diagnosis with no patient. The mount must be inside the producer's lifetime, and the reason must return IN-BAND so the producer can repair and re-emit — the shape src/server.ts:643 → src/outputs.ts:638-639 already realizes for output_write.
(d) BEFORE IRREVERSIBILITY, NOT AT IT. Adjudication precedes every irreversible commitment (spend, child exit, durable write, phase advance), so a violation costs a re-emission rather than the chair's entire work. Late-and-atomic is what converts one absent field into total loss (src/runtime.ts:2176-2185 and the gate at :2252-2264 — atomicity is correct; the late mount is what makes it expensive).

WHY THIS IS THE KILLING INVARIANT AND NOT A WEAKER ONE: it is immune to all three obvious non-fixes. A retry policy re-runs a producer that was never told the reason (the child exited at src/claude_invoker.ts:705 before the mount at src/runtime.ts:2252). Strengthening the prompt cannot help — the effective schema is ALREADY in the prompt (src/claude_invoker.ts:199-202 via promptSchemaFor :92-98) and is precisely what the emission violated; that unification carried the owner's describing half into the prompt and stopped there. Relaxing the schema moves the boundary rather than enforcing it. Only relocating the mount closes the class.

DERIVED CLASS-GUARD OBLIGATION (binding on the fix-spec phase): the guard test must not assert 'extractJson validates'. It must assert the invariant structurally — for each site the sweep classified as an instance, feed a payload that satisfies shape/selection but violates the owned predicate, and assert the refusal is raised IN that frame, carries the owner's own reason string, and occurs with zero durable writes and zero post-producer-exit aborts. A guard that only tests the model-chair path re-instantiates the very error this class names: closing one coordinate instead of the relation.
